$description: Apollo Legacy override set (ADR-0011: themes = override sets at the semantic tier). Per-mode values Legacy re-binds OVER the Mono base; any path absent here falls back to Mono. Consumed by canon/gen_theme_cascade.py, which generates the [data-apollo-theme="legacy"] cascade into canon.css (AUTO-THEMES block) — root-level canonical vars + per-component vars via each snippet's #token-manifest. Never hand-edit canon.css; edit THIS file and re-run the generator. Every override carries $note provenance: these values are reconstructed from the R-D16/R-D18/R-D20 eviction records and the Legacy-era roles still in the store, NOT invented. Authored 2026-07-21 (build-out Phase 0); extended as Phase-1 per-component finalisation surfaces more Legacy-owned roles.

progress/complete.$note: DECLARED #176 (2026-08-14, s176 WORKING — Dave's word, NOT YET RATIFIED BY EYE) TO CLOSE A FALL-THROUGH. THE CLASS: a theme that MEANS a value must DECLARE it — inheriting the base by silence is indistinguishable from having no position, and the base can move under you. s175-D1 made progress/complete (the CONTINUOUS-quantity bar) ink-only in all four themes; Legacy declared nothing, so it fell through to the MONO ink #1A1A1A. That is the wrong ink for this theme: Legacy's body ink is Grey 8 #333333 (col25-011, 'white or Grey 8 ONLY'; see this file's text/default), and #1A1A1A is the Mono digital-black. The bar was reading Mono's ink under a Legacy skin purely because nobody wrote the sentence down. This override writes it down. LIGHT #333333 = Legacy ink, a CHANGE from the inherited #1A1A1A. DARK #FFFFFF = UNCHANGED from the base, and declared anyway — that is the whole point of the class: an agreeing value still has to be stated, or the agreement is an accident. Values are LITERALS, deliberately not an $alias onto text/default, so a future move of Legacy's body ink does not silently drag the progress bar with it; a rebind would be Dave's, not a side effect. Sole consumer: Progress-bar (the discrete-step components bind step/complete, which is a different token and a different rule).

step/complete.$note: Evicted from the Mono base 2026-07-21 (Dave, Phase-1: 'resolve this to the newer red status color' — worker-A receipt F3; reconfirmed same evening on the harness: 'the colours in legacy … are fine'). Pre-eviction base values (were $alias color/primary, flat #DB0011 both modes). R-D19: #DB0011 is Legacy's alone. MOVED #175 (2026-08-14, s175-D1) from path progress/complete to path step/complete — values UNCHANGED, so Legacy's step indicators render byte-identically. progress/complete (the continuous-quantity bar) now takes the ink pair in all four themes; Dave: 'the other ruling was a miscommunication.' Legacy colour on the DISCRETE-STEP indicators is DEFINITE, not inherited: 'these will have colours in legacy for sure.' | #176 (2026-08-14, s176 WORKING — Dave's word, NOT YET RATIFIED BY EYE) RE-VALUED, AND THE ONLY THEME THAT DOES NOT INHERIT. Dave verbatim: 'I think we should exactly the same system that we use for the success roundels on all, they can just inherit then wholesale. Except Legacy, it uses the red in light mode and white in dark.' The base step/complete now aliases rag/success (the roundel chain), so Mono/Console/Supercharge take the success green; Legacy alone keeps a red. THE RED IS THE LEGACY ERROR RED, NOT THE BRAND RED: Dave first said 'the red', then said 'warning red', then corrected himself verbatim — 'Legacy error, sorry my mistake'. So light = #A8000B (this theme's rag/error, value-identical, declared as a literal here because Legacy's error red is stable in both modes and this token must NOT follow a future rag/error move without Dave). Dark = #FFFFFF, which is the RAG ROUNDEL POLICY leg Dave named ('white in dark') — the same policy Confirmation already carries (dark roundels go WHITE, the mark knocks to the black page). Prior values RETIRED TO THIS NOTE, not deleted: light #DB0011 / dark #DB0011 (the R-D19 brand red, moved here from progress/complete by s175-D1). ⛔ NOT #DB0011 (brand), ⛔ NOT #FFBB33 (Legacy amber) — both were said aloud and both were withdrawn. | #176 REFINEMENT, RULED OFF THE LIVE REVIEW PAGE (2026-08-14, still WORKING): LIGHT IS BACK TO THE PRIMARY RED #DB0011. Dave, seeing reviews/STEP-SUCCESS-SYSTEM-2026-08-14-v1.html with his own eye: 'Use the primary red for Legacy.' THE FULL SEQUENCE, RECORDED BY ADDITION so no leg is lost and no leg is re-litigated: (1) #DB0011 both modes — s175-D1, the R-D19 brand red carried over from progress/complete; (2) #A8000B light / #FFFFFF dark — #176 in CHAT, Dave correcting himself twice, ending 'Legacy error, sorry my mistake'; (3) #DB0011 light / #FFFFFF dark — #176 RULED OFF THE RENDERED PAGE, which outranks the chat leg: leg (2) was chosen from a description, leg (3) from the thing itself. THE DARK LEG #FFFFFF IS UNTOUCHED BY THIS REFINEMENT — 'white in dark' still stands, Dave did not revisit it. So #A8000B is now the RETIRED value here (it remains Legacy's rag/error, untouched, in its own path) and #DB0011 is the LIVE one — the reverse of what leg (2) inscribed, and deliberately so. ⛔ Do not 'restore' #A8000B from the sentence above: read the sequence to its end.

step/on-complete.$note: MINTED #176 (2026-08-14, s176 WORKING — Dave's word, NOT YET RATIFIED BY EYE). LEGACY IS THE ONE THEME THAT MUST OVERRIDE THE STEP MARK, because it is the one theme whose step fill is NOT the success fill. ⛔ THE MARK POLICY BINDS TO THE FILL, NOT TO THE TOKEN NAME. LIGHT #FFFFFF: this MATCHES LEGACY'S OWN ROUNDEL MARK EXACTLY — apollo-legacy marks/success and marks/error are both #FFFFFF (s122-D5, 'knockout on the Legacy error fill #A8000B' / 'on the Legacy success fill #00847F'), so a white tick on Legacy's red is the roundel system doing what it already does, not a new invention. On the live fill #DB0011 that measures 5.25:1 — a gated leg, and it passes. DARK #1A1A1A: ⚠⚠ THIS LEG IS A DECLARED EXCEPTION AND IS **NOT RULED BY DAVE** — flagged loudly, on purpose. Matching Legacy's roundel mark 'exactly' would put #FFFFFF here, and Legacy's step fill in dark is ALSO #FFFFFF ('white in dark'), so an exact match renders a WHITE TICK ON A WHITE DISC — a glyph with 1:1 contrast, i.e. no glyph at all. Dave's own doctrine forbids that outcome in the same breath that it relaxes the decoration: 'the label and the symbol must carry the contrast not the decoration.' The SYMBOL is the channel; it cannot be invisible. So this lane inverts the mark for Legacy dark ONLY, to the same dark ink the other three themes use (#1A1A1A on #FFFFFF = 17.4:1), and SURFACES IT RATHER THAN BURYING IT: Dave never spoke to the Legacy dark GLYPH, only to the Legacy dark FILL. It is his to confirm or replace. This is a declaration, not an inheritance — the fall-through class again: a theme that means a value must say so.

badge/background.$note: Dave 2026-07-21, badge ruling on the harness (verbatim): 'the colours are fine apart from Legacy, it should be the legacy primary red on both light and dark.' Brand-PRIMARY red flat, deliberately NOT the Legacy error pair — that is why the badge/background component slot exists. Known fidelity condition: white numeral on #DB0011 ≈ 4.02:1 (< 4.5 text) — same Legacy-fidelity-vs-AA family as text/on-success white-on-teal, queued for Dave with that item.

motion/press/travel.$note: B-D7 (Dave 2026-07-22): press/hover MOVEMENT is ABSENT in Legacy — state feedback is colour-only (the as-built system has no scale physics; R-D24 reproduction posture). travel=0 makes scale(calc(1 ± 0/size)) the identity. Theme dial — raise if finessing ever wants it.

motion/press/darken.$note: B-D7: no :active brightness darken in Legacy — the pressed colour tokens carry the state. brightness(1) = no-op.

$guardsNote: s158-D1 (Dave, #158): GUARDS. Not token overrides — declarations that THIS theme keeps a paint a later MONO-ONLY ruling moved away from it. They were hand-edited into canon.css's AUTO-THEMES block (which says do NOT hand-edit), and that is what held gen_theme_cascade --check red. Sourced here so the generator emits them and canon.css is clean generated output again. Provenance: .cn-banner .banner.err ink + .cn-tabs --badge-bg/--badge-ink = s149-D1 clauses (1) and (3), scoped 'this is right for mono only' — legacy s131-D1 / console+supercharge s132-D1 stay as built; --error-atom: var(--error) = s151-D1, an explicit NO-OP guard so the two-red law's atom fork cannot reach a theme that owns its own red. placement 'sorted' joins the sorted declaration namespace, 'append' is emitted after it in authored order (both reproduce the ratified bytes).
